topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the course structure, themes, and learning outcomes for cancer biology.

topics.label: Disruption of genetic programming and tissue architecture in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer originates from accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue organization.

topics.label: Mechanisms and pathology of tumor invasion, metastasis, and progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the pathological distinctions between benign and malignant neoplasms, focusing on mechanisms of local tissue invasion, metastatic spread, and stepwise tumor progression.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and clinical pathophysiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the systematic naming of tumors and explain the physiological mechanisms through which neoplastic growths cause illness and death.

topics.label: Patterns of cancer incidence across human populations and animal taxa
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze the epidemiological distribution of major cancer types in humans and compare tumor incidence across diverse multicellular species.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and screening strategies for cancer detection
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine typical clinical cancer signs and evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of population screening methods across different tumor sites.

topics.label: Lecture closing and housekeeping
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture with concluding remarks and reminders for upcoming practicals and lectures.
